questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
1. Access to  nature experiences and opportunities. 
2. it was important to me that I was able to speak the local language. 
3. I was eager to explore the norwegian way of having university and understand more of norwegian culture. 

Erasmus+ made it possible for me economicly, because Norway is for sure expensive.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
Everything happens in the center, so you should be okay with the logistics needed when you can't go home so easily. 
However life outside city center is more calm and closer to nature, which I enjoyed a lot!

questions.answer:
Similar to Copenhagen
However I had "shcool exaams" without help. So you had to remember things by heart. One was 8 hours -  so the type of exam is a bit more challenging compared to what i'm used to.

questions.answer:

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I liked all the courses and can recommend all of them. 

Especially I liked: "The Frontier of Anthropological Research: Contested". It was a phd candidate presenting the newest research, which was so interesting. He was also in general very good at presenting his work.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There are a lot of student associations. For instance I really enjoyed being a part of "Studentersamfunnet", where they organised events every week. My favorite was "Tuesday meeting", which was a gathering at the liberary with breakfast and a talk about a topic. Such a good way to gather with other students.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
All you could imagine: 

Photography
Sport
Politics
Art 
Music

There is a day in the beginning where all the clubs present their association. So it's very accessable

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I recommend joining a student association for instance "Studentersamfunnet". This is a good way of getting to know the local students

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
So many amazing things in the area: 

1. Hikes: Fløyen, Ulrikken, Løvstakken, Stolzen
2. Skiing: Kvamskogen (so close and great for skiing). 
3. Museums: The art museums are great: KODE
4.  Cabin trips (the cabins are amazing!).

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Take classes in Norwegian

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: My experience is that norwegians are a bit more introvert than danish people, so my best tip is to be patient. - And it's worth it. Norwegian friends are the best!

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer:
Many Norwgians are very good at using the nature around them. 

I also really loved the trust everybody had to each other. A very good moral in the society. I always felt very save.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Enjoy the small things: be curious about the food (pinnekjøt, skolebolle, Rømmegrød), the language differences, the culture, the student life, the people, the nature: then it for sure will be a good experience. 

2. Don't do things to tick something off in a box. Quality over Quantity: what matters is the people you are experiencing things with and how you are feeling yourself. Not how many hikes or cities you get to see. 

3. Be open and flexible: many things is happening during an exchange. But also remember "you-time" I recommend "tid for yoga": yogaplace in the city.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Use DNT and become a member: then you can go on beautiful Cabin trips. 
BSI are  arranging trips, so you don't have to be an outdoor expert.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer:
The nature experiences 
The friendships 
Learning the language
The courses

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer:
Saying goodbye :)
- and a bit of fomo. 

But luckely Bergen is not so far away.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer:
I'm very grateful for my exchange og and I recommend a lot! 

I recommend to go with train: it's a beautiful and climate friendly solution :) It only takes 1 day.
Interail pass wirgh 4 days of travelling during the 6 months is 900 (for Erasmus students), which is cheaper than flights. 

All the best! 
Enjoy
